prose: Bone-dry instrument air extracted natural moisture from the 150mm oak-tanned leather piston cup. The sealing lip curled inward away from the cylinder wall, allowing 6.5 bar air to bypass the piston and stalling the emergency blast damper halfway closed.

Hard magnetite scale particles carried through un-filtered air lines lodged beneath the piston follower plate. The trapped debris plowed 0.8mm deep longitudinal scoring grooves down the mirror-honed cast iron bore, causing continuous pneumatic hiss and pressure loss.

Misalignment of the 125mm piston rod caused the tapered brass cushion spear to enter the head deceleration pocket off-center. The brass spear galled tightly inside the mating steel sleeve, jamming the heavy armored blast door at 95% full travel.

Vacuum-impregnating molded steer-hide piston cups with a hot compounding of castor oil, beeswax, and colloidal flake graphite created a self-lubricating seal. The packing demonstrated zero stick-slip and sustained over 250,000 cycles without pressure bleed.

Radiant heat from the nearby foundry crucible furnace heated one side of the 160mm air cylinder to 180°C. The unequal thermal elongation stretched the two exposed steel tie rods, blowing out the rear cylinder head gasket in a deafening burst of compressed air.

Spring-loaded segmented bronze rod scraper rings mounted ahead of the rod gland packing scraped radioactive silica fallout dust and frozen ice off the 40mm hard-chrome piston rod. The scraper prevented abrasive grit from entering the internal cylinder barrel.

Flexural fatigue in the synthetic rubber shuttle diaphragm of the quick-exhaust valve tore the rubber flapper away from its center brass rivet. The ruptured valve prevented rapid cylinder decompression, increasing piston return stroke time from 0.4s to 4.2s.
